description: Cases an SDK is REQUIRED to skip, so `check_case_pinning.py --sdk <name>` does not report them as gaps. A deliberate per-SDK skip and a forgotten case look identical from outside; only the fixture knows which it is, so the reason is recorded here alongside the fixture text that states it. This list does NOT affect the default question — whether ANY driver runs the case — which a genuinely dead case still fails.

allow.why: The case's own `legacy_key_by_sdk.python` is null and its `skip_when_legacy_key_is_null` note states that apcore-python MUST NOT gain the fallback: no Python deployment ever had `observability.redaction.*` honoured, so adding it would create a deprecated surface for zero users, and a stale `observability.redaction.sensitive_keys: []` would flip from 'ignored, defaults apply' to 'key-based redaction disabled'. apcore-rust and apcore-typescript both pin it.

PIPELINE_HANDLER_NOT_SUPPORTED is raised only by apcore-rust, which cannot dynamically load a `handler:` target (DECLARATIVE_CONFIG_SPEC §4.4 records the per-SDK split). apcore-python supports `handler:` and therefore has no such error to raise, so its driver is REQUIRED to skip. apcore-typescript likewise supports it. The case's old apcore-python handling was `else: pytest.skip("Unknown error_code")`, which read as deliberate while checking nothing — that fallback is now pytest.fail, and this entry records the one skip that is genuinely correct.
